title: Matter / Burn Out

description.main: Daisuke Yokota's record of burning his own installation Matter after its 2015 showing in Xiamen, published by artbeat publishers, Tokyo, in September 2016 in an edition of 1,000. A 304-page wordless sequence of the fire and ash, processed from some 4,000 frames.
description.extended:
Matter / Burn Out is Daisuke Yokota's record of the burning of his own installation Matter, published by artbeat publishers, Tokyo, in September 2016 in an edition of 1,000 copies.

Matter is an installation of long rolls of photographic paper printed with Yokota's images and heaped through the gallery. It was shown in changing forms at Unseen in Amsterdam (2013), Photo London (2015) and Jimei x Arles in Xiamen (2015). When the Xiamen show closed, Yokota moved the rolls to a vacant lot nearby and set them alight. He photographed the fire and the ash in some 4,000 frames, then processed and edited them into this book. The 304 softcover pages run as a wordless sequence of grainy, high-contrast frames of flame, smoke and charred paper, with a folded caption sheet laid in. Shigeo Goto edited and produced the book and Goshi Uhira designed it. It was released with the exhibition MATTER / at G/P gallery, Tokyo, and the work was later shortlisted for the Prix Pictet Fire cycle.

Yokota, born in Saitama in 1983, treats photography as a physical material. He rephotographs, boils, scorches and wax-coats his prints. His installations pile the photograph up as matter to be handled and destroyed, among them the 100,000 waxed prints shown at the Aichi Triennale in 2016. This book sits between the black-and-white monographs Site/Cloud (2013) and Taratine (2015) and that installation work.
description.artist_bio: Daisuke Yokota (b. 1983, Saitama) lives and works in Tokyo. Known for reworked, degraded black-and-white photographs and for installations that treat the print as physical matter, including 100,000 wax-coated prints at the Aichi Triennale 2016. Books include Site/Cloud (G/P Gallery, 2013), Vertigo (Newfave, 2014) and Taratine (Session Press, 2015).
description.exhibition_context: Released alongside the solo exhibition MATTER / at G/P gallery Ebisu and Shinonome, Tokyo, opening 3 September 2016. The Matter installation it records was shown at Jimei x Arles International Photography Festival, Xiamen, 2015, and burned after the show closed.
